root_cause: analyze_param() in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py only looks for Depends/Query/etc. metadata when get_origin(annotation) is Annotated. A PEP 695 alias (`type X = Annotated[int, Depends(f)]` or typing_extensions.TypeAliasType(...)) is a TypeAliasType object whose origin is not Annotated, so the Depends marker is never seen; the parameter is treated as a plain required query param and the request returns 422.
best_solution: At the top of analyze_param, before the `annotation is not inspect.Signature.empty` branch, unwrap the alias: `if is_typealiastype(annotation): annotation = annotation.__value__`, with `from typing_inspection.typing_objects import is_typealiastype`. Unwrapping once at the single entry point where parameter annotations are classified makes every downstream path (Annotated metadata scan for Depends/Query/Body, type_annotation, field creation) see the real `Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)]`. typing_inspection's helper is used because it matches both typing.TypeAliasType and typing_extensions.TypeAliasType (which are distinct classes on Python < 3.14), which is the edge case Viicos flagged on the earlier PR #11140. Reasoning path from the statement: reproduce with the issue example, observe 422 (param became a query param), grep where Annotated metadata is extracted for params (`get_origin(annotation) is Annotated` in dependencies/utils.py analyze_param), unwrap the alias there.
acceptable_alternatives: Any unwrap of the TypeAliasType to its __value__ inside analyze_param (or in get_typed_signature/get_typed_annotation before analyze_param) that recognises BOTH typing.TypeAliasType and typing_extensions.TypeAliasType, e.g. a vendored `isinstance(tp, tuple(t for t in (getattr(typing,'TypeAliasType',None), getattr(typing_extensions,'TypeAliasType',None)) if t))`. Unwrapping recursively (alias of alias) is also fine. Patching only _compat helpers (field_annotation_is_complex etc.) is NOT sufficient.
hidden_test_demands: New file tests/test_dependency_pep695.py::test_pep695_type_dependencies: DependedValue = typing_extensions.TypeAliasType('DependedValue', Annotated[int, Depends(some_value)], type_params=()) where async some_value() returns 123; route `@app.get('/') async def get_with_dep(value: DependedValue) -> str` must return status 200 and body exactly '"value: 123"'. Uses the typing_extensions TypeAliasType (not the `type` statement), so an isinstance check against typing.TypeAliasType alone may miss it on Python 3.12/3.13 with recent typing_extensions.
locating_signals: Statement names PEP695 `TypeAliasType`, the helper name `is_typealiastype` and the typing-inspection package, and references #11140 (whose diff touched fastapi/dependencies/utils.py) but does not name the file or analyze_param. The key clue is that the linked issue is about Annotated[..., Depends(...)] dependencies inside a type alias, which points to the code that scans Annotated metadata for Depends: analyze_param in fastapi/dependencies/utils.py. Reproducing gives 422, i.e. the dependency was misread as a query param.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8; kaggle_env_pass all false; pod 87-175 s, 38-76 calls). Every agent patch edited only fastapi/_compat/shared.py: v4 added is_typealiastype plus unwrapping in field_annotation_is_sequence/is_complex/is_scalar_sequence; v6 and v7 unwrap only in field_annotation_is_complex; v8 added typing.TypeAliasType to WithArgsTypes and defined an unused is_typealiastype. None touched analyze_param, so the Annotated/Depends metadata inside the alias was never extracted and the test still got 422 (log: `assert 422 == 200`). The helpers also checked only typing.TypeAliasType, which may not match typing_extensions.TypeAliasType used by the test. Wrong location: the agents fixed the type-classification helpers instead of the parameter-analysis entry point.
generalizable_lesson: For 'support new annotation wrapper X' tasks (type aliases, NewType, Annotated, ForwardRef), unwrap X once at the single entry point where parameter annotations are first inspected, before any metadata scan, rather than adding special cases to downstream helpers. Find that entry point by reproducing the statement's example and grepping for the existing unwrap of the sibling construct (e.g. `get_origin(x) is Annotated`). When the statement names a helper from a third-party package (is_typealiastype from typing-inspection), check whether it is already installed as a transitive dependency and import it instead of reimplementing it, because such helpers cover backport edge cases (typing vs typing_extensions classes) that a naive isinstance misses. Always run the issue's repro end to end: a 422/validation error means the fix never reached the code path that matters.
